conventions.view: `jobs` (§10.8) with the ordering keys added at R-NEXT. Checked as ORDERING and RELEASE rather than membership: which jobs are blocked, by what, and which dispositions of a blocker free its dependents.
conventions.args: `ns` is the program namespace. Offsets are chosen at the transitions, because a fixture checked only at head cannot distinguish a rule from a coincidence.
conventions.expect: `ready` is open, unheld, and unblocked, in id order. `blocked_by` maps a job id (as a string) to its LIVE blockers. `forest` is the `part-of` breakdown and is asserted alongside so that a board conflating the two relations fails visibly.

checks.why: THE RULING. The campaign #4 is OPEN and its children #5 and #6 are both READY and neither blocked — §12.7 makes any subset of the children claimable. A board reading `part-of` as blocked-by returns ready=[2,3,4,10,11] here, omitting exactly the children the edge exists to make claimable. Also: #10's blocker #9 was REPLACED at #11, and a replaced blocker releases.

A TAKEN BLOCKER STILL BLOCKS. #3 is claimed at #12, so it leaves `ready` — but #7 is still blocked by it. Being worked is not being finished, and a board that treats a live holder as a release frees #7 here.

BREAKDOWN AND ORDERING ARE INDEPENDENT. #5 is a campaign CHILD and also #8's blocker; closing it releases #8 while the forest is unchanged. A board deriving one relation from the other cannot produce this row.

A CLOSED BLOCKER RELEASES, and closing #3 also returns it from `taken` — so #7 becomes ready and nothing is blocked. The DAG is empty here because everything is released, which must be distinguishable from the DAG being empty because nobody posted edges.

must_not.rule: A `part-of` target MUST NEVER appear in `blocked_by`. #5 and #6 are children of the open campaign #4 at every offset and are never blocked by it. This is the single rule the whole fixture is built around.

`blocked_by` and `forest` MUST NOT be derived from each other. At offset 13 the forest is unchanged while #8's blocker is released; at offset 11 #8 is gated on a campaign child, so a job may be ordered against work it is not part of.

A blocker with a LIVE HOLDER MUST NOT release its dependents. At offset 12 #3 is taken and #7 stays blocked. Taken-ness and released-ness are different questions and only `closes`/`supersedes` answer the second.
`ready` MUST NOT include held work. #3 is ready at offset 11 and absent at 12 with no other change than the CLAIM.

A job with no edges at all (#2) MUST be ready at every offset. Absence of ordering is not ordering, and a board defaulting unstated jobs to blocked would strand every job posted before this convention existed.
An out-of-range `at` MUST NOT be answered with a crash. Not asserted by the checks above because it is a defect filed rather than fixed here — `jobs` raises where `state` returns an empty answer.
